constraintText: Use no text or watermark. Add no borders, frames, cards, or presentation masks. Include one character only, with no extra subjects or scenery. Use no fragile lines, sharp tips, unnecessary outlines, tiny details, or decorative marks. Add no photorealistic material, dramatic bevel, glossy hotspot, deep occlusion, extrusion, strong three-dimensional rendering, or external cast shadow. Keep the background solid and uniform, with no texture, vignette, or lighting variation.

variants.label: H1
variants.rationale: 以画眉的眼圈和眉纹表现鸣禽身份
variants.prompt:
Create one complete full-bleed 1:1 square image, approximately 1536 × 1536.
Background: fill the entire square with solid #B8CFCA muted sage teal. Keep this background visible in every open area and in the corners not occupied by the character; the assigned emergence corner must be occupied by the character.
Subject: one extremely simplified, cute, endearing baby Chinese hwamei songbird character, with one soft rounded continuous plump silhouette. Its single defining feature is the hwamei's eye-ring continuing into a broad backward eyebrow sweep: simplify this into two broad soft round-ended eye patches with short wide swept ends, one around each eye. Both eye patches must be visible. Make the patches broad clean masses, never thin lines. A very short blunt rounded beak is integrated into the face; no pointed tips. Two small rounded wings merge into the body silhouette, both visible. No individual feathers, crest, feet, tail, headphones or other accessories.
Complexity: only 4–7 large basic shapes, at most two broad internal color regions. Two simple eyes, no mouth. Remove every nonessential line, anatomical detail, texture, and decoration. Readable at 32 × 32.
Color behavior: exactly three semantic colors total: two character colors plus the background. Use #A97247 warm chestnut brown for the whole head, body and wings; use #F7E8BE cream ivory for both broad eye patches and the tiny blunt beak. Use the body color for the small eye dots inside the eye patches. The entire eye-ring-and-brow treatment and tiny blunt beak use the secondary color, no third character color.
Composition: upright character emerging from lower-left, filling about 85–95% of the square. Cropping at bottom or assigned side is welcome. Preserve both eye patches and both wings in the visible composition. Never center or bottom-center the character.
Style: simplification, cuteness and lovable baby-like appeal, large head, compact proportions, soft cheeks, thick rounded contours, ultra-clean graphic treatment. Prefer one clear shape over several explanatory details. Add an extremely, extremely subtle, almost imperceptible sense of depth through a barely-there neo-skeuomorphic treatment.
Finish: only the character on the full-canvas background with normal square outer corners.
Constraints: Use no text or watermark. Add no borders, frames, cards, or presentation masks. Include one character only, with no extra subjects or scenery. Use no fragile lines, sharp tips, unnecessary outlines, tiny details, or decorative marks. Add no photorealistic material, dramatic bevel, glossy hotspot, deep occlusion, extrusion, strong three-dimensional rendering, or external cast shadow. Keep the background solid and uniform, with no texture, vignette, or lighting variation.
